setlist.title: Beat It On Down The Line

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Around And Around** (3 reviews): Carries much of the energy and several classic bends of the previous night's performance; Offered as a rebuttal to a critic who said the band mishandled Chuck Berry songs; compared with 10-06-77 [4][8][9]
- **Deal** (2 reviews): Jerry takes two choruses, seems finished, then switches to chords for a third pass that builds excitement; Jerry sings with direct, sincere communication, giving a feeling of personal connection [4][9]
- **Dupree's Diamond Blues** (2 reviews): Weir leads the pack at times in this song, per the audience mix; Jerry's voice, close to back to normal, is demonstrated by this reading [5][7]
- **Black Peter** (2 reviews): Builds to an incredible climax; Features a shredding crescendo [8][9]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): Runs over nine minutes and is called a crusher, alongside Deal [14]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Reviewer calls it one of the best ever, with the band exploding [8]

## The recordings

- **gd78-02-04.aud.vernon.12199.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 146 min; rated 3.75/5 by 16 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording lets each player be heard, with Weir sometimes out front, as in Dupree's; Jerry's voice is ragged; Not the greatest audience tape, but the playing comes through; Keith and Donna are especially good; Imperfect recording, but thick and completely listenable [5][6][7][10][11][14]
- **gd1978-02-04.132719.sbd.betty-latvala-bertrando.reel.wise.flac16**: soundboard; 9 songs; 83 min; rated 4.67/5 by 9 [2]
- **gd1978-02-04.122949.candyman.mtx.seamons.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 1 songs; 7 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Energy was unbelievable; many songs lack endings as the band flowed from one to the next [11]
- Deal is not a standard four-chorus version like the following night's; Around And Around has energy and bends like the previous night's JB Goode [4]
- Reviewer says the band was outstanding every show from Eugene through this run, after something shifted on 1/22 [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd78-02-04.aud.vernon.12199.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Reviewer is transferring the show from their father's tapes plus a dub found on a shelf; Hunter Seamons has a Candyman matrix incorporating a Dan Healy soundboard; Audience source transferred through MC, R, C, DAT, CDR, EAC to CD; remastered via Owens Brothers Vault [1][11][14]
- **gd1978-02-04.132719.sbd.betty-latvala-bertrando.reel.wise.flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by Dick Latvala and Jim Wise and Rob Bertrando; source: Set 2 Only; 7 Inch Half Track Nagra Reel Master @ 7.5 IPS; Recorded By Betty; Analog to Digital:By Dick Latvala(Technics 1506 Reel 2 Reel-Sony PCM R-500 DAT @… [2]. Also: Soundboard source from a reel, credited to Betty Latvala Bertrando, with Wise as the flac16 uploader [2]
- **gd1978-02-04.122949.candyman.mtx.seamons.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Partial 1 song Matrix by Hunter Seamons; Soundboard recording by Dan Healy; Audience recording transferred by Raoul Duke [3]
